Subject: Clarify charges for stitched conversations / rounding behavior

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Meridian is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Before we move to a pilot, finance asked a couple of specific billing questions that would affect how we size the pilot:

1) We stitch together multiple model calls in our pipeline (embedding -> reranker -> chat) and keep a running conversation-level context that we pass back into the chat model every call. Will we be double-billed for the same context tokens if they are included in successive requests within a short window? How does Redwood deduplicate / charge repeated prefixes?

2) Your docs mention a "billing quantum" and rounding minimums. What quantum do you apply for generation tokens and for embeddings? Is there any different treatment when calls include long contexts (e.g., 100k tokens) that are largely prefix reuse?

For reference, I've attached a small usage snapshot and one page of our current invoice where the numbers don't map to our expected utilization. If you can point us to the exact rounding math and whether an exception / credit is possible for the pilot, that will speed procurement.

Best,
Alice

Short answer up front: Redwood bills per request (request-level token accounting), and there is a rounding quantum applied to charged units. That can cause apparent double-counting when long prefixes are re-sent across many requests. There are a couple of mitigations we can propose for the pilot — see Karthik below.

Vanessa and I can also prepare a one-page invoice walkthrough for procurement. Karthik — can you confirm the current quantums for generate vs embedding and whether we can apply a conversation-level dedupe credit for a pilot?

Hi all — quick technical / policy write-up to make this explicit and propose our pilot exception.

1) Billing primitives and quantum
- Every request is tokenized and we account separately for prompt (input) tokens and completion (output) tokens. Embeddings are measured as a distinct call type and billed per-embedding-unit.
- Current production quantum: generation billing is rounded up to the nearest 64-token unit; embeddings are rounded up to the nearest 128-token unit (this is to align with our batching and GPU kernel amortization).
- There is also a per-request minimum of one quantum (so any request that tokenizes to 1-64 generate tokens will bill as 64).

2) Long-context behavior
- We do not compress or deduplicate prefixes at the service edge by default — each request that includes the same prefix will be billed independently. The reason is that model inputs are opaque at the routing layer and requests can be routed to different hardware pools / model variants.
- We do maintain an optional KV-prefix cache for Dedicated customers that can avoid re-sending large KV entries; however, charge reconciliation still sees the request payload unless the customer routes through our prefix-proxy (private deployments) which can instrument de-duplication.

3) Why you see "double" charges
- In stitched pipelines, a prefix passed through embedding/reranker stages and then again to chat will show up in invoice lines for each call type. On top of that, the 64-token quantum can amplify the delta when prefixes are near quantum boundaries.

4) Pilot exception / proposed playbook (what we can offer to Meridian)
- Conversation dedupe credit: For the 90-day pilot we can apply a conversation-level dedupe credit to invoice lines. Implementation: Meridian provides a conversation-id header for requests (or we can map by session id on our side). After the billing window we reconcile requests with identical conversation ids and identical prefix hashes within a 24-hour window, and we apply a credit equal to the duplicated prompt quanta. This is an off-invoice credit (line-item) — does not change base billing behavior after pilot.
- Reduced quantum for embeddings: for the pilot only we can bill embeddings at a 64-token quantum instead of 128, to reduce rounding friction for small embeddings-heavy pipelines.
- One-off invoice walkthrough: Vanessa and I will produce a sample invoice showing pre-credit vs post-credit numbers so procurement can sign off.

5) Operational caveats
- Conversation-id is required for reliable reconciliation. If you cannot provide that, we can attempt a best-effort prefix-hash match but it increases reconciliation noise.
- Credits will be reconciled and applied monthly; we will cap pilot credits to $25k unless otherwise approved by finance.

If Meridian is OK with the approach, Vanessa and I will draft the pilot SOW language and I will route the credit cap for finance approval.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
